questions.question: In an equilateral triangle inradius is 4 cm. What is the circumradius?
questions.solution:
Given:

An equilateral triangle inradius is 4 cm.

Concept used:

In equilateral triangle, 

Circumradius = a/√ 3

Inradius of equilateral triangle = a/2√ 3

**Calculation:**

Inradius of equilateral triangle = 4

⇒ a/2√ 3 = 4

⇒ a = 8√3

Circumradius = a/√ 3 = 8√3/√3

⇒ 8

questions.question: Sides of a triangle are 12 cm, 9 cm and 9 cm. What is the radius of the circumcircle of this triangle?
questions.solution:
Given:

The sides of a triangle are 12 cm, 9 cm, and 9 cm

Formula used:

Area of the triangle = √[s (s – a) (s – b) (s – c)] where s = (a + b + c)/2

Circum-radius of the triangle = abc/[4 × area of triangle]

Calculation:

Area of the triangle = √[s (s – a) (s – b) (s – c)] where s = (a + b + c)/2

Side of the triangle are, a = 12 cm, b = 9 cm and c = 9 cm, then

s = (12 + 9 + 9)/2 = 30/2 = 15 cm

Area of the triangle = √[15 (15 – 12) (15 – 9) (15 – 9)] = √[15 × 3 × 6 × 6] = √5 × 6 × 3 = 18√5 cm2

As we know,

Circum-radius of the triangle = abc/[4 × area of triangle] = (12 × 9 × 9)/(4 × 18√5) = (27√5)/10

∴ Option 3 is the correct answer.

questions.question: In an isosceles triangle ABC, AB = AC and AD is perpendicular to BC. If AD = 12 cm and the perimeter of ΔABC is 36 cm, then the length of BC (in cm) is
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The altitude of 12 cm divides the isosceles triangle into two congruent right-angled triangles.

Recall the common Pythagorean triplet with a perpendicular of 12: **(5, 12, 13)**.

Let equal side (hypotenuse) = 13 cm and half-base = 5 cm.

Verify perimeter: 13 + 13 + (2 × 5) = 36 cm, which exactly matches the given condition.

Therefore, the total length of base BC is 2 × 5 = 10 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 10 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ ΔABC is isosceles with equal sides AB = AC = x.

⇒ AD ⊥ BC, and for an isosceles triangle, altitude AD bisects the base.

⇒ Let BD = DC = y, making the full base BC = 2y.

⇒ Perimeter of ΔABC = AB + AC + BC = 2x + 2y = 36 cm.

⇒ Divide the perimeter equation by 2: x + y = 18.

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Pythagoras Theorem: Hypotenuse² = Perpendicular² + Base²

**Calculations:**

⇒ In right-angled ΔABD, apply the Pythagoras theorem:

⇒ AB² = AD² + BD²

⇒ x² = 12² + y²

⇒ x² − y² = 144

⇒ Expand using algebraic identity: (x + y)(x − y) = 144

⇒ Substitute (x + y) = 18 into the equation:

⇒ 18 × (x − y) = 144

⇒ x − y = 144 ÷ 18 = 8

⇒ To find y, subtract the new equation from the initial sum equation:

⇒ (x + y) − (x − y) = 18 − 8

⇒ 2y = 10 cm

⇒ Since the base BC is represented by 2y, length of BC = 10 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 10 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of Isosceles Triangle

In an isosceles triangle, the altitude drawn to the unequal side always bisects both the base and the vertex angle. This property effectively divides the main triangle into two congruent right-angled triangles.

Area of Isosceles Triangle

The formula to find the area is Area = (b ÷ 4) × √(4a² − b²), where 'a' is the length of equal sides and 'b' is the length of the base. Alternatively, if altitude is given, Area = ½ × base × height.

Pythagorean Triplets

Memorizing common integer triplets (a, b, c) where a² + b² = c² is a crucial time-saving tool in exams. Examples include (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), (8, 15, 17), and (7, 24, 25). These scale up proportionally as well.

questions.question: Median of an equilateral triangle is 15√3** **cm. What is the side of this triangle?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Median of an equilateral triangle is 15√3 cm.

**Concept Used:**

Length of median of the equilateral triangle = (√3/2) × side

**Calculation:**

Let the side of the equilateral triangle be a cm.

Length of median of the triangle = (√3/2) × a

⇒ (√3/2) × a = 15√3

⇒ a = 30 cm

Side = 30 cm

**∴ Option 3 is the correct answer.**

questions.question: In a triangle PQR, QR is produced to S. If ∠PRS = (9x - 15)°, ∠RPQ = (2x)°, and ∠PQR = (4x + 15)°, what is the value of x?

In a triangle PQR, QR is produced to S.

If ∠PRS = (9x - 15)°, ∠RPQ = (2x)°, and ∠PQR = (4x + 15)°,

**Concept used:**

∠PRS = ∠RPQ + ∠PQR

**Calculation: **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/267a0cf81dfff5ae59a4a38e77a527376434066d9845b726a68afae82e81c066.png] 

∠PRS = ∠RPQ + ∠PQR

⇒ (9x - 15)° = (4x + 15)° + 2x

⇒ 9x - 6x = 30°

⇒ x = 10°

questions.question: In an equilateral triangle ABC, P is the centroid of this triangle. Side of ΔABC is 16√3 cm. What is the distance of point P from side BC?
questions.solution:
Given:

Side of triangle = 16√3 cm

Centroid = P

Concept used:

Height of equilateral triangle = √3/2 × a (where a is the side of the triangle)

Centroid divides median in the ratio of 2 : 1.

Calculations:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/66058a8e7cc0d836c4b5cc50f24160fe3a4ada6af96e83f6677fcddd77912ef4.png] 

⇒ Height = AD = √3/2 × a 

⇒ Height = √3/2 × 16√3

⇒ AD = 24 cm

⇒ AP : PD = 2 : 1

Let, AP = 2x

PD = x, AD = 3x

⇒ 3x = 24

⇒ x = 8

∴ The value of PD is 8 cm.

**∴ Option 1 is the correct answer.**

questions.question: The centroid of an equilateral ΔXYZ is L. If XY = 12 cm, then the length of XL in cm), is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

ΔXYZ is equilateral.

Side XY = 12 cm

'L' is centroid of ΔXYZ

**Concept:**

In equilateral triangles, angle bisector, median, perpendicular bisector are all same. The centroid lies on the median/angle bisector/perpendicular bisector of the triangle. In any triangle, the centroid is 2/3 along the median.

**Formula used:**

Median of equilateral triangle = (√3/2) × a, where 'a' is side.

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/45bd0abe1daf0fc0b65449d016d32cfd187ca71363243fe7c6da178dd1219203.png] 

IN ΔXYZ

Median XM = (√3/2) × 12 = 6√3 cm

∵ L is the centroid;

∴ XL = (2/3) × (XM)

∴ XL = (2/3) × 6√3

⇒ XL = 4√3 cm

**∴ The answer is 4√3 cm.**

questions.question: L is the incentre of ΔONP. If ∠OLP + ∠ONP = 195 degree, then what will be the value of ∠OLP?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/08d313bc05e74e3d67f9093a4795245054a0446663b6ca5a48a59125fbfc507d.png] 

∠OLP + ∠ONP = 195

∠OLP = 195 - ∠ONP

L is the incentre.

∠OLP = 90° + ∠ONP/2

195 - ∠ONP = 90° + ∠ONP/2

105 = 3∠ONP/2

∠ONP = 70°

∠OLP = 195 - 70 

∠OLP = 125°

**∴ Option 4 is the correct answer.**

questions.question: The sides AB and AC of △ABC are produced to points D and E, respectively. The bisectors of ∠CBD and ∠BCE meet at P. If ∠A = 72°, then the measure of ∠P is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5b32e885f0e27866f9da1826717cc9f891d69ced3576826d58e3531674c6c0a8.png] 

Let ∠DBP = ∠PBC = a°

And also ∠ECP + ∠PCB = b°

∠ABC = 180° - 2a° and ∠ACB = 180° - 2b°

In ΔABC,

180° - 2a° + 72° + 180° - 2b° = 180°

a° + b° = 126°

In ΔPBC,

a° + b° + x° = 180°

x° = 180° - 126° = 54°

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a63c93e11c1bd5840d125804b189a0e6fab4be6ad12b4d33c13eace1e72ac42b.png] 

∠BPC = 90° - (1/2) × ∠A

Here, ∠A = 72° 

∴ ∠BPC = 90° - (1/2) × 72° 

⇒ ∠BPC = 90° - 36° = 54°

questions.question: In ΔXYZ, if G is the centroid and XL is the median with a length 18 cm, then the length XG is:
questions.solution:
**Given :**

XL is the centroid of a triangle XYZ and G is the centroid of the median 

**Concept used :**

In a triangle ABC if a median AD is drawn from A to side C, then centroid G divides the AD in the ratio 2 : 1

**Calculations :**

XL = XG + GL

XG: GL = 2: 1 (G is the centroid)

⇒ XG = (2/3) of XL 

⇒ XG = (2/3) × 18

⇒ XG = 12 

∴ **XG is 12 cm.**

questions.question: In a ΔABC, O is the orthocenter of this triangle. ∠B = 55 degrees and ∠BOC = 120 degrees. What is the value of ∠ACB?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

In a ΔABC, O is the orthocenter of this triangle

∠B = 55 degrees and ∠BOC = 120 degrees.

**Concept Used:**

The sum of all the angles in quadrilateral = 360 degree

Orthocentre: It is the point where the perpendicular is drawn from the vertices to the opposite

sides of the triangle intersect each other 

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bb8937eb80be8b7f5f2606b5d21f2f53beb92ffca5530c49391dc12aa0b6ecb5.png] 

If in triangle ABC, BE and CD are altitudes and they intersect at O then,

 ∠ODA = ∠OEA = 90 and ∠BOC = ∠DOE = 120

 In quadrilateral ADOE 

⇒ ∠ ADO + ∠DOE + ∠OEA + ∠DAE = 360 

⇒ 90 + 120 + 90 + ∠ DAE = 360 

⇒ ∠DAE = 360 - ( 90 + 120 + 90) = 360 - 300 = 60 

Using Angle sum Property.

∠A + ∠B + ∠C = 180°

60 + 55 + ∠C = 180°

∠C = 180° - 115° = 65°

Therefore, ∠ACB = 65 degrees.

**∴ Option 2 is the correct answer.**

questions.solution:
**Given:**

Inradius of an equilateral triangle = 5√3 cm.

Concept: We'll use the formula of the inradius of an equilateral triangle which is a = 2√3r, where 'a' is the side length and 'r' is the inradius.

questions.question: In ∆ DEW, AB∥EW. If AD = 4 cm, DE = 12 cm and DW = 24 cm, then find the length of DB.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

In ∆DEW, AB∥EW.

AD = 4 cm, DE = 12 cm, DW = 24 cm.

**Formula Used:**

Using the Basic Proportionality Theorem (BPT):

If a line is drawn parallel to one side of a triangle to intersect the other two sides, then it divides those sides in the same ratio.

**Calculation:**

Using BPT, we have:

(AD)/(DE) = (DB)/(DW)

Substitute the given values:

(4)/(12) = (DB)/(24)

Simplify the ratio on the left side:

(1)/(3) = (DB)/(24)

Cross-multiply to solve for DB:

⇒ DB × 3 = 24

⇒ DB = 24 / 3

⇒ DB = 8 cm

**The length of DB is 8 cm.**

questions.question: In a ∆ABC, two medians AD and BE intersect at G at right angles. If AD = 18 cm and BE = 12 cm, then the length of BD is equal to:
questions.solution:
Given:

BD = DC (As AD is median)

AE = EC (As BE is median)

The length of AD = 18 cm

The length of BE = 12 cm

Concept used:

The medians of a triangle intersect each other at the centroid, which divides each median in the ratio 2:1.

Here, G is the centroid of the triangle.

Pythagorean theorem:-

H2 = P2 + B2

Calculation:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1600bbdd6e389266f663a699b0aae4c5816522e1b22835eb21d356ac34134feb.png] 

AG : GD = 2 : 1

Let AG and GD be 2x and x respectively. 

2x + x = 18

⇒ 3x = 18

⇒ x = 18/3

⇒ x = 6

⇒ GD = 6 cm

BG : GE = 2 : 1

Let BG and GE be y respectively.

2y + y = 12

⇒ 3y = 12

⇒ y = 12/3

⇒ y = 4

BG = 2 × 4 = 8 cm

In right-angled ΔBGD,

BD2 = BG2 + GD2 

⇒ BD2 = (8)2 + (6)2 

⇒ BD2 = 64 + 36

⇒ BD2 = 100

⇒ BD = 10

BD = 10 cm

∴ The length of BD (in cm) is 10.

questions.question: O is the incentre of the ΔPQR. If ∠POR = 120 degree, then what is the ∠PQR?
questions.solution:
**Given Data:**

∠POR = 120 degree

**Formula:**

The incenter of a triangle is equally inclined to all the sides of the triangle.

Angle at incentre = 90° + vertex angle/2

**Solution:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e262e79f2c52b00ab525cddf698eb5eb72bac6d07a0e95f7c6bd562f5416e413.png] 

⇒ ∠POR = 120° 

⇒ ∠POR = 90° + ∠PQR/2

⇒ 120° = 90 + ∠PQR/2

⇒ ∠PQR/2 = 120 - 90

⇒ ∠PQR = 30° × 2 = 60° 

**Hence, ΔPQR is 60°. **

questions.question: The three medians AX, BY and CZ of Δ ABC intersect at point L. If the area of Δ ABC is 30 cm², then the area of the quardrilateral BXLZ is:
questions.solution:

Area of ΔABC = 30 cm²

**Formula used: **

When three medians of Δ ABC intersect at point L

Area of ΔBLX = 1/6 × ΔABC

**Calculation: **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4b688d243fbebaf2dec84a0de1a96c84e7ef02434f8fa09e9da3ce46f45f9826.png] 

Area of ΔBLX = 1/6 × ΔABC 

⇒ Area of ΔBLX = 1/6 × 30

⇒ Area of ΔBLX = 5 cm²

Area of BXLZ = 2 × ΔBLX

⇒ Area of BXLZ = 2 × 5

⇒ Area of BXLZ = 10 cm²

**∴**** The area of the quadrilateral BXLZ is 10 cm²**

In a triangle MNO, XA, XB and XC are perpendicular bisectors on sides MN, ON and OM

respectively intersect each other at X.

∠NMO = 55° 

**Concept Used:**

If O is the circumcenter of the △ABC then the angle made at the circumcenter by joining any

two vertices of the triangle is twice the angle at the third vertex of the triangle i.e. the angle

made at the circumference at the circle.

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c6445f0b2ebde4b8a10b55a05562ef6e2eefb898d7d07443b3598a197f3724d5.png] 

∠NXO is the angle made at the circumcenter of the triangle.

So,

∠NXO = 2 × ∠NMO

∠NXO = 2 × 55°

∠NXO = 110° 

**∴ Option 2 is the correct answer.**
